USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is 3-SAT and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = ThreeSat
3-SAT.

Instance: {"num_vars": m, "clauses": [[l1, l2, l3], ...]}
  * Variables are 1..m. A literal is +v (v is true) or -v (v is false).
  * Every clause has exactly 3 literals on 3 different variables, so a
    clause may not repeat a variable or contain both v and -v.
  * Literal order inside a clause and clause order do not matter. The
    same clause may appear more than once.
  * Variables need not all appear in a clause.

Yes iff some assignment of true/false to variables 1..m makes every
clause contain at least one true literal.

Edge cases: a formula with no clauses is satisfiable (yes), for any m,
including m = 0. A formula with clauses needs m >= 3.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-s_1v01l0

It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-s_1v01l0 && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Vertex Cover.

Given a 3-CNF formula with m variables and c clauses, build a graph:

  * For each variable v in 1..m, a "variable gadget": two vertices
      pos(v) = 2*(v-1)        representing literal  +v
      neg(v) = 2*(v-1) + 1    representing literal  -v
    joined by an edge.  Any vertex cover must contain at least one of them.

  * For each clause i (0-based), a "clause gadget": three new vertices
      clause_base(i) + 0, + 1, + 2
    forming a triangle.  Any vertex cover must contain at least two of them.
    Each of the three vertices is connected to the variable-gadget vertex
    for the corresponding literal occurrence.

Set k = m + 2*c.  A satisfying assignment yields a cover of size m + 2c by
taking the true literal vertex of each variable gadget and exactly two
vertices from each clause triangle (omitting one whose literal is true).
Conversely, a cover of size at most m + 2c must take exactly one vertex per
variable gadget and exactly two per clause triangle; the omitted triangle
vertex must be adjacent to a chosen literal vertex, which makes that literal
true, so the induced assignment satisfies every clause.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Map a 3-SAT instance to a Vertex Cover instance."""
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    edges = []

    # Variable gadgets: one edge per variable, forcing a truth choice.
    for v in range(1, num_vars + 1):
        pos = 2 * (v - 1)
        neg = pos + 1
        edges.append([pos, neg])

    def literal_vertex(literal):
        v = abs(literal)
        base = 2 * (v - 1)
        return base if literal > 0 else base + 1

    # Clause gadgets: a triangle per clause, plus links to literal vertices.
    clause_vertex_count = 3 * len(clauses)
    for index, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        base = 2 * num_vars + 3 * index
        a, b, c = base, base + 1, base + 2
        edges.append([a, b])
        edges.append([b, c])
        edges.append([a, c])
        for offset, literal in enumerate(clause):
            edges.append([base + offset, literal_vertex(literal)])

    n = 2 * num_vars + clause_vertex_count
    k = num_vars + 2 * len(clauses)
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": k}
EOF

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT to Vertex Cover.

Given a 3-CNF formula with m variables and c clauses, build a graph:

  * For each variable v in 1..m, a "variable gadget": two vertices
      pos(v) = 2*(v-1)        representing literal  +v
      neg(v) = 2*(v-1) + 1    representing literal  -v
    joined by an edge.  Any vertex cover must contain at least one of them.

  * For each clause i (0-based), a "clause gadget": three new vertices
      clause_base(i) + 0, + 1, + 2
    forming a triangle.  Any vertex cover must contain at least two of them.
    Each of the three vertices is connected to the variable-gadget vertex
    for the corresponding literal occurrence.

Set k = m + 2*c.  A satisfying assignment yields a cover of size m + 2c by
taking the true literal vertex of each variable gadget and exactly two
vertices from each clause triangle (omitting one whose literal is true).
Conversely, a cover of size at most m + 2c must take exactly one vertex per
variable gadget and exactly two per clause triangle; the omitted triangle
vertex must be adjacent to a chosen literal vertex, which makes that literal
true, so the induced assignment satisfies every clause.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Map a 3-SAT instance to a Vertex Cover instance."""
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    edges = []

    # Variable gadgets: one edge per variable, forcing a truth choice.
    for v in range(1, num_vars + 1):
        pos = 2 * (v - 1)
        neg = pos + 1
        edges.append([pos, neg])

    def literal_vertex(literal):
        v = abs(literal)
        base = 2 * (v - 1)
        return base if literal > 0 else base + 1

    # Clause gadgets: a triangle per clause, plus links to literal vertices.
    clause_vertex_count = 3 * len(clauses)
    for index, clause in enumerate(clauses):
        base = 2 * num_vars + 3 * index
        a, b, c = base, base + 1, base + 2
        edges.append([a, b])
        edges.append([b, c])
        edges.append([a, c])
        for offset, literal in enumerate(clause):
            edges.append([base + offset, literal_vertex(literal)])

    n = 2 * num_vars + clause_vertex_count
    k = num_vars + 2 * len(clauses)
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": k}
EOF
